audits.title: Chlamydia in a district general hospital: an audit of treatment and contact tracing.
audits.standard: Central audit group guidelines on chlamydia management
audits.setting: Genitourinary medicine department, Dryburn Hospital, North Durham Healthcare NHS Trust (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Contact tracing of current and recent partners was more successful than of previous partners; women treated before attending were more likely to need retreatment.

audits.other_findings: Tracing of casual and previous partners has limited success against the new guideline standards.
audits.citation: White C, Wardropper AG. Chlamydia in a district general hospital: an audit of treatment and contact tracing. Int J STD AIDS. 1999;10(1):57-59. doi:10.1258/0956462991912953. PMID: 10215133.

audits.title: A multidistrict audit on the management of Chlamydia trachomatis in genitourinary medicine clinics in Yorkshire.
audits.standard: 100% of chlamydia-positive patients treated within 2 weeks; 100% return for test of cure within one month; 100% referred for contact tracing
audits.setting: Nine GUM clinics (one teaching hospital, 8 district general hospitals), Yorkshire Deanery

cycle1.result: 89% treated within 2 weeks; 64% returned for test of cure within one month; 93% referred for contact tracing.

audits.intervention: Changes in practice and a region-wide multidisciplinary audit initiative (not detailed).
audits.citation: Monteiro EF, Harris J, Gilliatt P. A multidistrict audit on the management of Chlamydia trachomatis in genitourinary medicine clinics in Yorkshire. Int J STD AIDS. 1997;8(12):792-795. doi:10.1258/0956462971919147. PMID: 9433957.

audits.title: Re-audit of referral compliance of chlamydia-positive women from a family planning clinic.
audits.standard: Care pathway for referral and treatment of chlamydia-positive women
audits.setting: The Palatine Centre family planning clinic and GUM clinics, Manchester

cycle1.result: Treatment verified in 90% (n=89); 85% (n=84) attended GUM; median referral to treatment 5-6 days; sexual contacts traced in 57% (n=56).

audits.other_findings: Described as a re-audit but no earlier results are given; partner notification was the weak area.
audits.citation: Siddiqui F, Kirkman RJ, Chandiok S. Re-audit of referral compliance of chlamydia-positive women from a family planning clinic. J Fam Plann Reprod Health Care. 2004;30(2):86-87. doi:10.1783/147118904322995429. PMID: 15086990.

audits.title: The management of Chlamydia trachomatis in genitourinary medicine clinics: a national audit in 2004.
audits.standard: National outcome standards for chlamydia management
audits.setting: Genitourinary medicine clinics across the UK (national audit)

cycle1.result: 99% (1647) treated appropriately; 76% (1261) followed up, of whom 12% needed re-treatment; 71% (1186) managed appropriately within four weeks; 942 partners (0.56 per index case) managed within four weeks.

audits.other_findings: Partner notification was more successful when the index patient was followed up (P<0.0001); outcomes were associated with ethnicity.
audits.citation: Challenor R, Pinsent S, Chandramani S, Theobald N, Daniels D. The management of Chlamydia trachomatis in genitourinary medicine clinics: a national audit in 2004. Int J STD AIDS. 2005;16(7):494-499. doi:10.1258/0956462054308431. PMID: 16004630.

audits.title: UK National Audit of chlamydial infection management in sexual health clinics. case notes audit: information-giving, partner notification and follow-up.
audits.standard: UK National Guideline for chlamydial infection
audits.setting: UK sexual health clinics (national case notes audit)

cycle1.result: Partner notification advice given to 91%, method documented in 92%; outcome not documented in about 25%; contacts screened per index 0.52 outside London and 0.29 in London, below guideline levels.

audits.other_findings: Only half given written information; about a quarter had no follow-up.

UK National Audit of chlamydial infection management in sexual health clinics. case notes audit: information-giving, partner notification and follow-up. audits.title: UK National Audit of chlamydial infection management in sexual health clinics. clinic policies audit.
audits.standard: UK National Guideline for chlamydial infection
audits.setting: 177 UK sexual health clinics (clinic policies audit)

cycle1.result: 92% had nucleic acid tests; 97% had leaflets, 30% lacking antibiotic and contraception information; about two-thirds followed recommended test of cure interval.

audits.other_findings: Only 18% routinely asked patients to reattend; 86% of 146 English clinics had a local screening programme coordinator.
audits.citation: Carne C, McClean H, Bhaduri S, Bunting P, Fernandes A, Dhar J, et al.. UK National Audit of chlamydial infection management in sexual health clinics. clinic policies audit. Int J STD AIDS. 2008;19(7):477-479. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2008.008139. PMID: 18574121.

audits.title: Managing chlamydia infections in young men: results from an audit of a public men's clinic in New York City.
audits.standard: Not stated; timely treatment, partner management and retesting for reinfection
audits.setting: Young men's public clinic, New York City

cycle1.result: 99% treated, 81% within 14 days; 65% had no documented partner management; of 34% with a later visit only 36% retested.

audits.citation: Jones HE, Pressman EJ, Bell DL, Kerns JL, Lykes ST, Garth J, et al.. Managing chlamydia infections in young men: results from an audit of a public men's clinic in New York City. Int J STD AIDS. 2011;22(10):581-584. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2011.010462. PMID: 21998179.

audits.title: Chlamydial partner notification in the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH) 2011 UK national audit against the BASHH Medical Foundation for AIDS and Sexual Health Sexually Transmitted Infections Management Standards.
audits.standard: BASHH/MedFASH STI Management Standards: ≥0.6 contacts seen per index case outside London, ≥0.4 in London
audits.setting: Level 3 and level 2 sexual health clinics, UK (BASHH 2011 national audit)

cycle1.result: Level 3: 43% (regional range 0-80%) of clinics outside London met ≥0.6 and 85% (82-88%) in London met ≥0.4; level 2: 39% outside London and 43% in London met the standards.

audits.other_findings: New standards proposed for index-reported (≥0.6) and healthcare-worker-verified (≥0.4) contacts within four weeks.
audits.citation: McClean H, Carne CA, Sullivan AK, Radcliffe KW, Ahmed-Jushuf I, National Audit Group of British Association for Sexual Health and HIV. Chlamydial partner notification in the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH) 2011 UK national audit against the BASHH Medical Foundation for AIDS and Sexual Health Sexually Transmitted Infections Management Standards. Int J STD AIDS. 2012;23(10):748-752. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2012.012035. PMID: 23104751.

audits.title: 2019 British Association of Sexual Health and HIV National Clinical Audit of timelines to be seen, test results and treatment for Chlamydia trachomatis.
audits.standard: BASHH/MEDFASH Standards for the Management of Sexual Health Services 2014: seen within 2 working days, results within 10 working days, lab report within 5 working days, treatment within 3 weeks
audits.setting: UK level 2 and level 3 sexual health clinics (221 sites), national audit

cycle1.result: 92.1% had attempted notification within 10 working days of a positive test; 94.0% treated within 15 working days of result; GUM/level 3 attenders seen within 2 working days, results within 10 working days and treatment within 3 weeks met the standard; offer of being seen within 2 working days and lab report within 5 working days did not.

audits.other_findings: 32% of sites had no specified lab turnaround time; mean walk-in turn-away rate 6.1%.
audits.citation: Fitzgerald N, Anderson ER, Apea V, Curtis H, Goodall L. 2019 British Association of Sexual Health and HIV National Clinical Audit of timelines to be seen, test results and treatment for Chlamydia trachomatis. Int J STD AIDS. 2022;33(6):604-607. doi:10.1177/09564624211059094. PMID: 35379055.
